items.name: OpenAI GPT-6 Cyber
items.summary: OpenAI's cyber-specialised variant of GPT-6 Astra, launched 5 November for vetted Daybreak Red defenders. It scores 48.5% on ExploitGym, is rated Critical for cybersecurity under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, and was used to find 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox flaws and build 948 working Linux kernel exploits in research.

items.name: Thinking Machines Lab Inkling 2 Small
items.summary: Mira Murati's lab launched its second-generation model on 5 November: a 594B-parameter sparse MoE with 17B active per token, built for long-horizon autonomous work. It scores 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and runs on Tinker today, with full weights promised under Apache 2.0 next week after safety testing.

items.name: Google Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
items.summary: Google's video generation and editing model went generally available on 5 November across the Gemini API, Vertex AI and Gemini for business. It creates and edits 15-second clips with native audio in multi-turn conversations, at $0.07 per second for 720p — 30% cheaper than Omni 1.1.

items.name: Moonshot AI Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.summary: Moonshot published the open weights of its 2.8T-parameter MoE on Hugging Face on 4 November — the largest open-weight model ever released, with 104B active parameters per token and a 1M-token context. It scores 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, near Claude Opus 5.5, though its custom licence gates large commercial API resellers.

items.name: OpenAI ChatGPT Images 2.6
items.summary: Launched 4 November across ChatGPT, Codex and the API, Images 2.6 adds animated GIF creation and reusable reference images, with generation about 50% faster. Developers get two new API models, GPT-Image-2.6 Flare for speed and Sunburst for detail, with GIF and SVG output.
